summary: 1933 ground-mounted L-4 cab in the Okanogan National Forest, reported gone by about 1957. Reached by a walk up from a locked gate; no source describes what remains now.

staffing.status: a lookout on duty in July 1937 put out a lightning fire; no staffing names in the sources read

access.note: Gated road. The summit is about half a mile up the road from a locked gate; no source says whether the gate is open to the public.

visit.trail_note: Walk about half a mile up the road from the locked gate, per WillhiteWeb. The cab was reported gone around 1957, and no source says whether anything remains to climb.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Okanogan National Forest
facts.status_note: Cab reported gone by about 1957; no source describes what remains at the site now

events.note: Panoramic images taken from the roof

Site appears to have been used in July 2001 in connection with the Thirty-mile Fire; road newly reworked and gate repaired with a new lock (2001 account)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites page says the cab was removed in the 1960s. WillhiteWeb (reported gone around 1957) and Fire Lookout (gone in 1957) give 1957. The story gives both dates.

notes_for_editor: Only the Forest Lookouts page cites the 1937 newspaper, and only through WillhiteWeb's quote of the Wenatchee Daily World; the paper itself was not read. The 2001 account is one quote by Irene Potter (dated 2001 on WillhiteWeb), repeated in the register; the story keeps the source's 'appeared' hedge. The gate's current status is not stated, so access is marked restricted. The SummitPost photo has no licence noted and no photo is added. Summit lookout mention rests on the photo caption.
